newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm on technical bounce.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm on technical bounce.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures shed a negative bias to end firmer on Friday, spurred by a technical rebound after the market's recent slide.
Sentiment was also heartened by buy-backs of banking stocks after news of Nippon Credit Bank's alliance with Bankers Trust.

"The market is trying to build a bottom. The consolidation is taking place over a span of about 600 points," a dealer with a European commission house said. He suggested prices could hover between 17,500 and 18,100 before breaking down again.
The June Nikkei contract ended up 220 points at 17,780 on a moderate turnover of 17,435 lots.
The yen's firmer tone in Asian markets on Friday was seen likely to limit the upside for the cash Nikkei index.
"A lot of oral intervention held the yen up. This will serve to merely cap the Nikkei," another local dealer said.
The yen's slide against the dollar, a favourable factor for exports, was being offset by weakness in the overall Japanese economy, particularly in the financial sector.
Some dealers said Friday's uptick was a pause in the longer-term downtrend toward more solid support at 16,850 points.
The MSCI Taiwan index saw mixed trade as the cash market failed to make further gains after Thursday's sharp rises.
April futures inched up to settle at 358.2, up 4.8 points, on a volume of 1,658 lots.
